written.myAnswer: The four whorls are calyx (sepals), corolla (petals), androecium (stamens), and gynoecium (carpels).

The diploid megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis to form four haploid megaspores; usually, only one survives. It undergoes mitotic divisions to form eight haploid nuclei. Two nuclei move to the centre and act as the polar nuclei; they fuse to form the fusion nucleus. Of the other six nuclei, one develops into the egg cell.

The male gametophyte is the pollen grain, formed from a microspore; it has a tube cell and a generative cell, which forms two sperms. The female gametophyte is the embryo sac, formed in the ovule; it contains an egg cell and a fusion nucleus.

The calyx is the outermost whorl made of green, leaf-like sepals that protect the inner parts of a developing flower. The corolla is the second whorl and is made of petals, which are coloured in most flowers.

A stamen is the male reproductive structure; it consists of an anther and a filament, and the anther contains pollen sacs. A carpel is the female reproductive structure; it consists of an ovary, style, and stigma, and ovules are produced in the ovary.

The sporophyte is the diploid generation that produces spores; the gametophyte is the haploid generation that produces gametes. Spores develop into gametophytes, and gametes fuse to form a zygote that develops into a sporophyte.

The diploid sporophyte produces haploid spores by meiosis. In flowering plants, microspores develop into pollen grains (male gametophytes), while a megaspore develops into the embryo sac (female gametophyte). These gametophytes produce gametes. During double fertilization, one sperm fuses with the egg to form a diploid zygote, and the other fuses with the fusion nucleus to form the triploid nucleus that develops into endosperm. The zygote develops into an embryo; the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit. A seed can grow into the next sporophyte.

The diploid megaspore mother cell in the ovule undergoes meiosis to produce four haploid megaspores, usually only one of which survives. The surviving megaspore undergoes mitosis to form eight haploid nuclei. Two become the polar nuclei in the centre and fuse to form the fusion nucleus; the other six form the egg cell and five other cells. The embryo sac is seven-celled and eight-nucleate.

Asexual reproduction generally produces offspring genetically identical to the parent and contributes little genetic variation. Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of gametes and creates genetic variation among offspring.

After a pollen grain lands on the stigma, its tube cell grows a pollen tube through the style toward the ovary. The tube enters an ovule, usually through the micropyle, and carries the two sperms to the embryo sac for double fertilization.
